neighbours.label: preposition after 'Once'/'got' marking arrival at a place ('Once in Chicago', 'got to Granby')
fire: After the long drive, once in Denver, we went straight to the hotel.
Once at the river, look for the shallow riffles near the bank.
When I finally got to Boston, the rain had stopped.
Once in Paris, she found a small apartment near the station.
Once at the summit, the climbers rested for an hour.
By the time we got to the farm, the cows had been milked.
Once in London, he took a job at a printing shop.
When they got to the village, the market was already closing.
quiet: After the long drive, we went straight to the hotel in Denver.
